channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: US Dollar: Staying strong as Fed expectations hold – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar’s resilience despite lower Oil prices and improved global risk sentiment, highlighting that hawkish Federal Reserve communication is keeping the Dollar supported.

item.title: British Pound holds steady against Japanese Yen after mixed UK PMIs
item.description: GBP/JPY trades around 209.90 on Wednesday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day with a modest 0.05% decline.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Cautious MNB stance supports HUF – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke reviews the Hungarian Central Bank decision to keep the key rate at 5.50% while lowering its medium-term inflation target to 2.5% from 2028. The MNB slightly raised its 2027 inflation forecast and will move to eight policy meetings per year.

item.title: Euro dips against Canadian Dollar following HCOB PMI data release
item.description: EUR/CAD halts its four day-winning streak, trading around 1.6090 during the European hours on Wednesday. The currency cross is under pressure as the Euro (EUR) holds losses following the release of the latest HCOB Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data for Germany and the broader Eurozone.

item.title: Euro remains depressed as German politics, France's debt offset strong PMI figures
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains on its back foot against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, extending its decline to two-and-a-half-month lows after dropping about 0.5% so far this week.

item.title: Euro flat lines above 180.00 vs weak Yen as German political turmoil offsets upbeat PMIs
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross seesaws between tepid gains/minor losses through the first half of the European session on Wednesday and moves little following the release of flash Eurozone PMIs.

item.title: Indian Rupee declines after two-day gain as hawkish Fed narrative dominates
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after rising in the past few trading days.

item.title: Swiss Franc: SNB preview signals steady policy – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee expects the Swiss National Bank to keep its policy rate unchanged at 0% at the September 24 meeting, despite higher energy prices and a modest uptick in headline inflation.

item.title: S&P Global PMIs expected to show resilient US economic growth in September
item.description: S&P Global will release on Wednesday its preliminary September Purchasing Managers' Indices (PMIs) for the United States, based on surveys of top private sector executives, to provide an early indication of economic momentum. The data is expected to highlight US economic resilience.

item.title: Dow Jones futures rise ahead of US PMI data
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain by 0.12% to trade near 52,350 during European hours on Wednesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures advance by 0.10% to trade around 7,840, while Nasdaq 100 futures inch higher 0.03% to trade near 31,040.

item.title: United Kingdom flash Services PMI expands slower-than-expected to 51.7 in September
item.description: The United Kingdom (UK) S&P Global Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) expands at a moderate pace to 51.7 in September. The data was already anticipated to arrive lower at 52.0 from 52.5 in August.

item.title: Oil: Geopolitics drive volatile price path – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Michael Every notes Oil prices are currently lower on hopes for de-escalation in multiple conflicts, including developments around Saudi infrastructure, Iran talks and Ukraine.

item.title: Australian Dollar slides to one-week low, below 0.7100 ahead of jobs data on Thursday
item.description: The AUD/USD pair comes under heavy selling pressure on Wednesday and weakens further below the 0.7100 mark, hitting a one-week low during the early part of the European session.

item.title: Gold approaches $4,300 as Fed hike bets boost USD to fresh high since late July
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its steady intraday slide through the first half of the European session on Wednesday, reversing a part of the previous day's recovery from sub-$4,300 levels.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Downside still favoured toward 158.40 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann maintain a constructive short-term view on USD/JPY after the pair closed at 157.37. They still see scope for further US Dollar (USD) strength, with intraday moves expected within 157.10–157.90 and firm resistance at 158.40.

item.title: Eurozone flash Manufacturing PMI remains steady at 52.7 in September
item.description: Preliminary HCOB Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) in the Eurozone remains steady at 52.7 in September, while it was expected to drop to 52.6. The Composite PMI unexpectedly rises to 53.1 from 52.0 in August.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah holds losses following BI rate decision
item.description: USD/IDR loses ground for the second successive day, trading around 17,850 during European hours on Wednesday. The pair holds losses as the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) remains subdued following the release of Bank Indonesia (BI) interest rate decision.

item.title: Euro remains muted after mixed German flash PMI data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains almost steady against its major currency peers after the release of the German preliminary HCOB Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data for September.

item.title: WTI Oil hovers at two-week lows near $89.00 awaiting Middle East developments
item.description: Oil prices maintain their negative trend on Wednesday, with the price of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel flatlining at the $89.00 area, its lowest level in nearly three weeks and 13% below last week’s highs.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: HUF outlook mixed after NBH pause – ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky says the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) delivered an expected pause in rate cuts and lowered its inflation target to 2.5%, creating a supportive backdrop for the Hungarian Forint.

item.title: Germany’s flash Manufacturing PMI unexpectedly drops to 53.8 in September
item.description: German flash HCOB Manufacturing PMI has come in lower at 53.8 in September. The data was expected to arrive higher at 54.5 from 54.3 in August. However, the overall business activity remain stronger-than-expected due to robust Services PMI data.

item.title: Equities: Flat close with sector rotation – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that United States (US) equities finished virtually flat, as strength in technology and semiconductor stocks offset a sharp decline in financials.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Eyes 1.4100 as bulls retain control near July 29 highs
item.description: The USD/CAD pair prolongs its weekly uptrend for the third straight day, hitting a fresh high since July 29 during the early part of the European session on Wednesday. Bulls now await a move beyond the 1.4100 round figure before positioning for further gains amid a supportive fundamental backdrop.

item.title: Euro nudges up against British Pound with Eurozone and UK PMIs in focus
item.description: The Euro (EUR) edges up against the British Pound (GBP) for the second consecutive day on Wednesday, although it remains halfway within recent ranges, with trading volumes at low levels, and investors awaiting Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data from the UK and the Eurozone.

item.title: Brent: Price slide extends on pipeline restart – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team notes Brent crude trading near USD 98/bbl after six straight sessions of declines, with Oil acting as the dominant intraday driver for broader markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines to near 0.5700 on hawkish Fed remarks ahead US PMI data
item.description: The NZD/USD pair declines to around 0.5710 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. Hawkish rhetoric from US Federal Reserve (Fed) officials regarding sticky US inflation provides some support to the US Dollar (USD) against the New Zealand Dollar (NZD).

item.title: British Pound: Testing support near 1.3300 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight tentative downside momentum in GBP/USD after the pair slipped to 1.3322 and closed at 1.3342. They see scope for a dip toward 1.3315, while judging 1.3300 as major support and potentially hard to break.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens further against US Dollar as hawkish Fed bets dominate
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to underperform against the US Dollar (USD), with the USD/JPY pair trading 0.2% higher to near 157.70 during the European session on Wednesday. The pair trades higher due to continued outperformance by the US Dollar.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar continues to gather strength ahead of PMI data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Wednesday, September 23:

item.title: Euro: De-escalation risk weighs on EUR against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen discusses EUR/USD in light of rising hopes for de-escalation in the Middle East. She notes the US Dollar (USD) has gained as rate expectations shifted in favor of the United States, with Euro Area inflation seen more energy-sensitive.
